newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures shed caution ahead of key U.S. economic data on Thursday and Friday to rise with robust U.S. bonds, settling up 0.36 and close to the day's earlier high.
Analysts said further gains for the 10-year future could be limited to the 131.10/16 zone but that, if breached, it could pass its contract high of 131.24.
"The Bund did not break through its 103.52 resistance and that kept the (French bond future) from staying above 131," one said.
Traders said the market seemed relatively calm about the possibility of German interest rate rises despite the mark's recent slide.

Pol-Louis Martin, economist at BNP, said the German economy was split between a dynamic export sector and weak internal demand and that the pattern should last through 1998. "In that context, depreciation of the mark is good for an upturn and far from a threat as far as prices are concerned," he said.
The view was shared by several others.
In the cash market, the yield on the 5.50 percent OAT due 2007 dropped to 5.42 percent from 5.47 with the spread versus the German equivalent unchanged at minus eight basis points.
September PIBOR interest rate contracts also finished slightly stronger, up one basis point at 96.52.
Analysts said the market would be eyeing key U.S. second quarter GDP data due on Thursday and French unemployment figures for the month of June due at 0645 GMT.
